notes: The Home Assistant Companion app for Android, on Google Play as io.homeassistant.companion.android and one of the largest actively-maintained open-source Compose codebases: :app alone declares 99 @Preview functions across settings, onboarding, Matter commissioning and the Wear-companion surfaces, with a house theme rather than stock Material. Ordinary Android Compose, single Gradle build at the repository root. One thing a reviewer should know about the build: the root build.gradle.kts calls dependencyLocking { lockAllConfigurations() } and the repository ships gradle.lockfile, so injecting the preview plugin adds modules the lock state does not describe. That is what COMPOSE_PREVIEW_WRITE_LOCKS / --write-locks in the reusable pipeline exists for; nothing is edited in the upstream checkout beyond Gradle regenerating its own lock state for the throwaway build. Licence: Apache-2.0. The build cannot configure without a google-services.json it does not commit: AndroidApplicationConventionPlugin applies the Google Services plugin to every application module, and :app died on processMinimalDebugGoogleServices before a preview was discovered. The pipeline writes a placeholder for the applicationIds named above — both flavours' debug ids are listed, so the stub survives the change of rendered variant described below. They are exact ids because the plugin does no prefix fallback, and they come from the upstream convention plugins (base io.homeassistant.companion.android, flavour suffix .minimal, build-type suffix .debug), not from guesswork. variant is fullDebug rather than the plugin's default debug. :app has minimal and full flavors, so there is no plain debug variant, and app/src/screenshotTest/ — which the preview plugin compiles, because it renders @Preview functions declared there — references SettingsWearOnboardingViewContent, a symbol that exists only in app/src/full/. minimalDebug therefore fails to compile those sources before a preview is rendered; fullDebug builds. stubGoogleServices already names the fullDebug applicationId alongside the minimal one, so the stub needs no change. Two runs settled this import. Run 76 showed variant=fullDebug is correct — the render configured, compiled and drew previews — but the 600s default cancelled a render still making progress, so renderTimeout is 1800; :app here is a whole shipping application, not a design-system module. Run 39 then completed the render inside that budget and rendered 830 of 852 previews, which is what the exclusions below are measured against. The 22 that fail do so for three unrelated reasons, and only the third is this project's own doing. (1) Ten previews of the HTTP auth dialog never reach idle — AppNotIdleException, 'Compose did not get idle after ~120000 attempts in 60 SECONDS' — which is an endlessly recomposing frame rather than a slow one, so no budget rescues it and each burns a minute of the budget failing. That is FrontendScreen's 'Content with HTTP auth dialog' and 'in error state' across four devices, plus the standalone PreviewHttpAuthDialog and PreviewHttpAuthDialogWithError. (2) Seven Media Player previews die on kotlin.NotImplementedError from FakePlayer.getApplicationLooper (FakePlayer.kt:32), an upstream TODO() that media3's PresentationState.observe calls; the upstream fake is simply incomplete for this path. (3) Five Glance app-widget previews (ScreenPreview and its four siblings) die on NoSuchMethodError for androidx.glance.appwidget.AppWidgetComposerKt.composeForPreview, thrown from OUR GlanceAppWidgetPreviewRenderer.kt:71. These previews are fine; the renderer is compiled against Glance 1.2.0 and this project uses a version whose signature differs. They are excluded only to unblock the import and are tracked as a renderer defect in compose-ai-tools#5056 — they should come back once that is fixed. The ids carry SPACES, not underscores ('FrontendScreen Content with HTTP auth dialog_foldable'); an earlier underscore-shaped guess taken from the PNG filenames matched nothing, which is why the Media Player entries name both spellings. The catalog spec references none of these previews, so the completeness gate is unaffected. One further wrinkle, now half resolved: these ids contain SPACES, and until compose-preview-imports#73 the entries here were flattened to a comma-joined string whose validator rejected a space outright ('must be preview-id patterns … no spaces'), so they could not be written literally at all. The '?' glob was used instead — the matcher compiles it to regex '.', which matches a space — at the cost of also matching any OTHER character in that position, so each pattern was broader than its author meant and stayed precise only because nothing else happened to collide. excludePreviewIds is now carried as a JSON array and reaches the render through a newline-delimited file, so the FrontendScreen entry is written exactly: '*.FrontendScreen Content with HTTP auth dialog*', which is what the ids actually read. The two Media Player entries keep their '?' form deliberately. Both spellings were listed here precisely because the separator was never confirmed for that group — an earlier underscore-shaped guess taken from the PNG filenames matched nothing — and the 22 reported ids that settled it are not recorded in this repository, so narrowing them to a literal is a guess that costs a 30-minute render to test. Convert them the next time this import's failing ids are in front of someone. The current set was checked against all 22 reported ids — all 22 match — and against ScreenPreviewOther, PreviewMatterCommissioningScreen and PreviewSettingWearLandingView, none of which match, so nothing the spec names is caught; replacing '?' with the literal space it stood for cannot widen that.
